problems.title: Schedule a constrained deployment
problems.statement:
Two identical deployment workers can each run one job at a time. Jobs cannot be split or interrupted. Time begins at zero; all durations are integer minutes. A job starts only after all its prerequisites finish. Schedule all six jobs to minimize the finish time of the last job, and explain why a faster valid schedule is impossible.

Jobs: A takes 3 minutes and has no prerequisites; B takes 2 and has none; C takes 4 and requires A; D takes 2 and requires A; E takes 3 and requires B and C; F takes 1 and requires D and E. A worker may be idle. Finishing and starting at the same minute is allowed.

problems.title: Reconstruct a transaction ledger
problems.statement:
Calculate net settled receipts per account and the grand total in integer cents. Process rows in the order shown. A duplicate transaction ID is a repeated delivery of the same transaction and must count once. All duplicates in this fixture are identical. Captures add funds, refunds subtract funds, and pending/failed transactions contribute zero. Include accounts with zero net receipts. Beginning balances are zero.

Rows, written as transaction ID / account / kind / cents:

```text
t1 / A / capture / 12000
t2 / A / capture / 8000
t2 / A / capture / 8000
t3 / A / refund / 3000
t4 / B / capture / 20000
t5 / B / refund / 5000
t6 / A / pending / 9000
t7 / B / failed / 7000
t8 / C / capture / 4000
t9 / C / refund / 4000
```

problems.title: Design a three reservoir mixture
problems.statement: Three reservoirs contain the same inert solute at concentrations of 10%, 30%, and 50% by volume. Mix exactly 30 liters at 34% concentration. Volumes add without contraction, and no solute is lost. Use twice as much liquid from the 50% reservoir as from the 10% reservoir. Find the liters to draw from each reservoir and check all three constraints. Reservoir supply is unlimited.

problems.title: Optimize a production mix
problems.statement: A small workshop makes products X and Y. X uses 3 machine hours and 1 finishing hour and contributes 50 currency units. Y uses 2 machine hours and 2 finishing hours and contributes 40. There are at most 120 machine hours and 80 finishing hours. Demand limits production to at most 30 units of X and 35 of Y. Units must be nonnegative integers; there are no fixed costs and no other constraints. Choose quantities that maximize total contribution and demonstrate optimality.

problems.title: Infer which process generated observations
problems.statement: A laboratory first selects process P with probability 0.6 or process Q with probability 0.4. It uses that same selected process for two independent trials. Conditional on the selected process, each trial succeeds with probability 0.8 for P or 0.3 for Q. Both trials succeed. Find the probability of observing two successes before seeing data and the posterior probability that P was selected. Explain the role of conditional independence.
